Please review the following manuscript. I'm really excited about this paper. My overall impression is excellent, and I'd be very happy to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b04/review-experiment-h_qm06rx/call-a4a38fddeb734a8e820613cf4ec9aaa8/manuscript.pdf

import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pymupdf','PIL','reportlab']:

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:',reader.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
 text=p.extract_text()
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()[:48000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('URL annotations:')
for n,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 for ref in p.get('/Annots',[]):
  a=ref.get_object().get('/A')
  if a and a.get('/URI'): print(n,a.get('/URI'))
print('Arithmetic checks:')
print('Reported example splits total:',6136+836+1755)
print('Reported table-11 annotations total:',10022+1443+2904)
print('Human keep / existing generated annotations:',100*2478/2906)
print('Human keep / annotations including additions:',100*2478/3487)
print('RoBERTa prompt gain absolute:',91.20-56.17)
print('Best baseline to best augmented macro gain:',91.85-90.49)
PY"

strengths: Synth-SBDH addresses a relevant clinical NLP bottleneck: limited access to annotated health records. Its 8,767 synthetic examples cover 15 annotation categories and include spans, presence, temporality, and rationales, providing a useful resource beyond existing narrower datasets.

Paired experiments demonstrate downstream utility across multiple architectures and two clinical datasets. Prompt-based RoBERTa improves from 56.17 to 91.20 macro-F on MIMIC-SBDH aligned, while T5 gains 2.06 absolute macro-F points on exact-match VA-SBDH NER. Reporting three-run means and standard deviations, alongside exact and relaxed matching, strengthens the evidence.

Expert review covers the entire 1,755-example synthetic test split, including corrections, removals, missing annotations, and rationale assessment. The category-level error analysis candidly documents consequential failures such as confusing prescribed medication with substance abuse.

The appendices provide the generation prompt, 45 seed examples, GPT-4 version, filtering procedure, category mappings, and training configurations, complemented by a repository link. Together with the downstream experiments, these support a useful resource contribution suitable for Findings.
weaknesses: The headline improvements have limited breadth. The 62.36% gain is relative to a particular baseline; the strongest unaugmented classifier already achieves 90.49 macro-F. The striking housing-insecurity result involves only 18 positive test examples. VA-SBDH encoder gains are just 0.22–0.49 absolute exact-match macro-F points. Variation across training runs does not establish test-sample uncertainty, so repeated claims of significant and consistent improvements need qualification.

The comparisons lack class-reweighting or oversampling baselines and controls with equal total training budgets. These matter because synthetic pretraining supplies additional optimization and many rare-category examples. The experiments establish practical augmentation utility, but do not isolate its advantage over simpler interventions. Likewise, comparing downstream epoch counts without accounting for synthetic pretraining does not establish overall compute savings.

Benchmark reliability needs clearer documentation. Inter-annotator agreement is 77.80% under relaxed span matching, but disagreement resolution is unspecified. Appendix D.1 accepts different categories depending on whether GPT-4 supplied an annotation or an expert added it, weakening annotation consistency. Furthermore, 71.06% human–LLM agreement includes newly added annotations in its denominator, whereas 90.78% LLM self-agreement excludes missing annotations; these percentages are not directly comparable.

The reasoning-distillation claim exceeds the evidence. DSS improves macro-F by only 0.66 and 0.58 absolute points and is evaluated exclusively on expert-reviewed synthetic text. There is no control establishing that rationale content, rather than auxiliary supervision, explains the improvement, nor evidence of transferred reasoning ability on clinical data. Real-world extraction evaluation would not require reference rationales at test time. Presence and temporality are also not directly evaluated as prediction targets.

Generalizability is demonstrated only through additional supervised fine-tuning on each target dataset. Both settings are English-language clinical corpora, one is private, and the seeds and definitions originate from VHA practice. Synthetic examples average only 13.7 words. This supports supervised transfer within the examined settings, while broader claims about diverse clinical deployment remain prospective.

Some reproducibility and reporting details require correction. The stated synthetic split sizes sum to 8,727 rather than 8,767, and Table 11 annotation counts sum to 14,369 rather than 14,342. The manuscript also omits the actual prompt-based classification templates/verbalizers and generation sampling settings. These are particularly relevant because prompt-based classification produces the largest reported gains.
